conf.description: cisco-asa vpn-aaa dataset, syslog-raw format (113xxx AAA + 722xxx AnyConnect/SVC families): parsing is deferred entirely to the Elastic cisco_asa integration (113xxx via an enumerated grok, 722xxx via a shared Group/User/IP pattern re-parsed per message ID). This pipeline is intentionally thin: it only tags event.dataset and passes _raw through untouched.

conf.comment: cisco-asa / vpn-aaa / syslog-raw: credential-attack evidence base for the VPN head-end. Do NOT re-parse user, reason, server, user-IP, Group/TunnelGroup/GroupPolicy, assigned IPv4, session type/duration/bytes, or Client Type here -- the Elastic cisco_asa integration owns the per-message-ID grammar for this family, including the 'None' user-IP drop and the AAA-server destination.ip-to-server.address rewrite (both documented as Elastic-side @custom pipeline steps in the map, not Cribl steps). The field table's only transform (message_id lookup) requires a field already extracted from the body, so it is not safely implementable pre-parse. The map's one concrete Cribl-side recommendation for this dataset -- conditionally masking usernames if policy requires it -- has no defined masking algorithm in the source map, so it is left for a future, explicitly-scoped pipeline revision rather than guessed here.

functions.description: document why this pipeline does not parse _raw
